passages.text: The toy study predicts small-molecule solubility with a graph model. Evaluation used a scaffold split of the fictional SolToy dataset. No external validation was performed and scaffold coverage was limited.

cases.source_ref: inline:E1 (fictional toy study; not a publication)

passages.text: The toy graph representation predicts a binary ADMET endpoint. Five-fold internal cross-validation used a random split of fictional ClassToy. On ClassToy random cross-validation, AUROC was 0.8 for the graph model versus 0.7 for fingerprints. The graph advantage disappeared under a scaffold split. Label imbalance and absence of external validation limit generalizability.

cases.title: SYNTHETIC: Toy docking and molecular dynamics
cases.source_ref: inline:E1 (fictional toy study; not a publication)

passages.text: The toy workflow ranks small molecules using docking and molecular dynamics. A single receptor conformation from fictional DockToy was used for docking. On DockToy, the candidate docking score was -8 kcal/mol versus -6 kcal/mol for the reference ligand. Molecular dynamics examined pose stability rather than binding affinity. No experimental binding assay was performed and receptor sampling was limited.
